title: What Podiatry Is All About
description: Podiatrists are doctors of podiatric medicine (DPM) who diagnose and treat conditions of the foot, ankle, and related leg structures. They handle bunions, heel pain, fractures, diabetic foot wounds, ingrown toenails, and perform foot and ankle surgery. Patients range from children with gait issues to athletes with injuries to seniors and diabetics needing preventive foot care. Podiatrists work in private practices, hospitals, sports clinics, nursing facilities, and the military. This record lays the foundation: the core purpose, the people it serves, and where it fits in everyday life.

title: History and Evolution
description: Chiropody, the predecessor of podiatry, dates back centuries; the first US school of chiropody opened in New York in 1911. The field became the Doctor of Podiatric Medicine degree in the mid-20th century, with surgical scope expanding as training standardized through accredited colleges and residencies. Knowing where the trade came from explains why things are done the way they are — and which 'rules' are just old habits.
key_points: History explains current practice.
